voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: A book no one has been able to read. In Prague, in the sixteen-sixties, a scholar sent it to Rome. His letter is still with it.
It was for Athanasius Kircher, who claimed to read Egyptian hieroglyphs. The letter says only he could read it.
It says Emperor Rudolf the Second was said to have paid six hundred ducats for it.
And that it was thought to be Roger Bacon's work. The writer would not vouch for that.
Its previous owner had written to Kircher too, and tried until he died. No reading from Kircher is on record.
